# Chapter 9-d — Group G: C-SACL

**Document:** `NH_MASTER-21_SYSTEM_BEHAVIOR_v0_1_CANDIDATE__CH09-d.md`  
**Status:** CANDIDATE  
**Source repository:** `nesgeva/NH-GOVERNANCE`  
**Source commit:** `6a7160ba688ba4e433a31899162815df7e2bab17`  

This piece contains SACL's session and stream records, ordered access gates, disclosure boundaries and failure responses, followed by the accepted output-delivery coordination mechanics. Existing privacy, PBR, retry and mode owners retain their identities. Biometric authority follows in CH09-e, full mode coordination in CH09-i and the wider B24 model mechanics in CH10-b.

[SOURCE CONFLICT: V10 §25.4 Gate 2 requires no disqualifying spoofing or imitation-risk flags. The following sentence and Option A say imitation_risk blocks Gate 1 only and preserves recognized_ness. Both statements remain explicit; this writer does not reconcile them.]

[SOURCE CONFLICT: B-INT-6 §7 and crash row 11 describe claim-before-attempt as proving no channel contact. Its §7C and row 11b use the exact durable-dispatch-intent boundary. The receipt §6 item 1 expressly identifies the latter as controlling. The receipt §6 item 2 likewise clarifies that the short uncertainty-record description lists two safe resend routes but omits the separate late-positive-confirmation route, which records delivery without resending. These are the source's own clarifications, not new writer decisions.]

[SOURCE CONFLICT: B-INT-6 §11 item 11 says fifteen crash boundaries; §10 prints rows 1–15 and 11b, sixteen rows. All sixteen are retained.]

[SOURCE CONFLICT: B24 §6.4-C4 uses terminal delivery_outcome_unknown for its delivery child and terminal_delivery_outcome_unknown for its parent when no further automatic action is authorized. B-INT-6 §6C makes its proposed delivery_unknown explicitly nonterminal with its own parent open. The owner-specific labels and parent scopes remain distinct here; no unified lifecycle or conversion between them is decided. The kernel preserves component-owned state rather than reclassifying it.]

### C-SACL — Speaker Access-Control Layer (§25.4)
Stamp: DESIGNED    Source: [V10 §25.4] [MAP C-SACL]

ALONE
- What it is: DESIGNED — The owner of speaker authorization: what the current speaker may receive or do. [V10 §25.4 / What SACL Is and Is Not]
- Takes in: DESIGNED — SIA assessments, independent biometric state and PBRs obtained through LMAC and Person-Boxes. [V10 §25.4 / Access Level Calculation] [V10 §25.4 / Permission Boundary Enforcement]
- Does: DESIGNED — Recalculates each stream on every SIA event through Gate 0, Gate 1, Gate 2, Gate 3 and guest fallback; calculates the active-stream shared minimum; limits retrieval and final disclosure while the complete mechanism remains active. [V10 §25.4]
- Gives out: DESIGNED — Current stream authorization, shared output ceiling, permitted categories, immediate discard signals and audit events. [V10 §25.4]
- Must never: DESIGNED — Assess identity, analyze acoustics, interpret meaning, retrieve content, generate output, read wellbeing tier state or let a speaker override protected safeguards. [V10 §25.4]
- Fails closed by: DESIGNED — Restart discards in-progress operations and sets every stream to guest; stale assessments downgrade above-guest streams and add assessment_stale; SIA failure sets all streams to guest with an immediate audit; PBR query failure makes Gate 3 guest. [V10 §25.4 / Failure, Stale Assessments, Fail-Closed]

TOGETHER
- Fed by: DESIGNED — C-SIA — Speaker Identity Assessment (§25.3): per-stream identity and acoustic-suspicion evidence; C-BAI — Biometric Authorization Interface (§25.6): independent biometric authority; C-7L — Person-Boxes (§7L): PBRs through the authorized query route. [V10 §25.4]
- Fed by: CANDIDATE — C-SACL.17 — Access operational records: protected calculation, gate, downgrade, discard and alert history. [MAP C-SACL]
- Gated by: DESIGNED — C-7Q — Privacy, Deletion, Sensitive-data (§7Q): privacy passes before the final access factor; C-WIS-SEP — Wellbeing / Identity / Security Separation (§25.5; cross-cutting): wellbeing never supplies access authority. [V10 §25.4 / Output Gate (Two Factors, Sequential)] [V10 §25.4 / Three Mechanisms Kept Separate]
- Gated by: DESIGNED — C-SACL.16 — Protected-core safeguards: seven unconditional boundaries apply to SACL. [V10 §25.4 / Protected-Core Rules (Unconditional)]
- Changes: DESIGNED — C-LMAC — Live Mechanism Access Coordinator (§26): bounds retrieval by access and categories; C-9 — Access/authentication model + voice I/O + phone modes (§9): supplies the current speaker ceiling and downgrade/discard boundary. [V10 §25.4 / Avoiding Indirect Disclosure] [MAP C-SACL]

ALONE
- What it is: ACCEPTED — The proposed lifecycle of one logical output parent, including unresolved delivery reality. [04/NH_B_INT_6_PRIVACY_FIRST_SACL_SECOND_OUTPUT_CHAIN_WIRING_v1_3_CANDIDATE.md §6C]
- Takes in: ACCEPTED — Ordered owner decisions, claim/attempt events and channel-owner outcome facts. [04/NH_B_INT_6_PRIVACY_FIRST_SACL_SECOND_OUTPUT_CHAIN_WIRING_v1_3_CANDIDATE.md §6C]
- Does: ACCEPTED — Advances through the proposed states requested → privacy_prefiltered → access_scoped → retrieved → formed → optional privacy_transform_required loop → privacy_final_passed → access_final_passed → fence_and_owner_versions_revalidated → delivery_claimed → attempt_started. It then records the evidenced result. Any nonterminal state except proposed delivery_unknown can become proposed discarded on restriction, proposed withheld when a gate refuses and nothing permitted remains, or proposed failed. [04/NH_B_INT_6_PRIVACY_FIRST_SACL_SECOND_OUTPUT_CHAIN_WIRING_v1_3_CANDIDATE.md §6C]
- Gives out: ACCEPTED — At most one winning proposed terminal result per parent: delivered, withheld, discarded or failed. Proposed delivery_unknown is protective and nonterminal, leaving the parent open. [04/NH_B_INT_6_PRIVACY_FIRST_SACL_SECOND_OUTPUT_CHAIN_WIRING_v1_3_CANDIDATE.md §6C]
- Must never: ACCEPTED — Silently turn unknown delivery into success or failure, resolve it from Ness's request, or use a later new user request to replay the uncertain operation. A later new request is a separate new output operation. [04/NH_B_INT_6_PRIVACY_FIRST_SACL_SECOND_OUTPUT_CHAIN_WIRING_v1_3_CANDIDATE.md §6C]
- Fails closed by: ACCEPTED — Unknown delivery leaves only through the four channel-fact cases below. Later restriction, close or restart blocks future retries and may remove payload availability, but cannot rewrite unknown world reality or prevent a late confirmation recording historical delivery. [04/NH_B_INT_6_PRIVACY_FIRST_SACL_SECOND_OUTPUT_CHAIN_WIRING_v1_3_CANDIDATE.md §6C]

### C-SACL.27 — Ordered dispatch and channel-owned delivery truth
Stamp: ACCEPTED    Source: [04/NH_B_INT_6_PRIVACY_FIRST_SACL_SECOND_OUTPUT_CHAIN_WIRING_v1_3_CANDIDATE.md §7] [04/NH_B_INT_6_PRIVACY_FIRST_SACL_SECOND_OUTPUT_CHAIN_WIRING_v1_3_CANDIDATE.md §7C]

ALONE
- What it is: ACCEPTED — The dispatch seam separating a reservation, an accepted handoff and confirmed delivery. [04/NH_B_INT_6_PRIVACY_FIRST_SACL_SECOND_OUTPUT_CHAIN_WIRING_v1_3_CANDIDATE.md §7]
- Takes in: ACCEPTED — Exact payload and gate references, current owner/fence facts, stable parent/key, one intended attempt and its fresh claim. [04/NH_B_INT_6_PRIVACY_FIRST_SACL_SECOND_OUTPUT_CHAIN_WIRING_v1_3_CANDIDATE.md §7C]
- Does: ACCEPTED — Revalidates; flushes the fresh claim; flushes dispatch intent; marks the claim spent once intent is durable; contacts the channel with the intended attempt and stable token; appends the attempt event when the channel accepts the handoff; records outcome only from channel-owner facts. A claim proves authorization/reservation, an attempt proves accepted handoff but no written or seen byte, and only positive channel acknowledgment proves confirmed delivery. [04/NH_B_INT_6_PRIVACY_FIRST_SACL_SECOND_OUTPUT_CHAIN_WIRING_v1_3_CANDIDATE.md §7] [04/NH_B_INT_6_PRIVACY_FIRST_SACL_SECOND_OUTPUT_CHAIN_WIRING_v1_3_CANDIDATE.md §7C]
- Gives out: ACCEPTED — Confirmed delivery, confirmed non-delivery or explicit uncertainty. The first actual channel write is irreversible exposure; the positive confirmation receipt is the durable confirmed-delivery point. Before the first write the content remains cancellable; after it the exposed bytes cannot be recalled. [04/NH_B_INT_6_PRIVACY_FIRST_SACL_SECOND_OUTPUT_CHAIN_WIRING_v1_3_CANDIDATE.md §7]
- Must never: ACCEPTED — Treat intent as a call, handoff as visibility or a local record alone as generic external delivery proof; assume universal atomic idempotent dispatch. A supported verified same-token atomic contract is recorded and used, never presumed. [04/NH_B_INT_6_PRIVACY_FIRST_SACL_SECOND_OUTPUT_CHAIN_WIRING_v1_3_CANDIDATE.md §7C]
- Fails closed by: ACCEPTED — Before durable intent, reuse requires an active claim, current bindings and an unbegun intended attempt. After durable intent without a provable result, enters proposed delivery_unknown even if proposed delivery_attempt_event is absent. Resend requires positive non-delivery proof or verified same-token deduplication plus fresh current checks. [04/NH_B_INT_6_PRIVACY_FIRST_SACL_SECOND_OUTPUT_CHAIN_WIRING_v1_3_CANDIDATE.md §7C]

### C-SACL.30 — Immediate restriction and scoped cancellation
Stamp: ACCEPTED    Source: [04/NH_B_INT_6_PRIVACY_FIRST_SACL_SECOND_OUTPUT_CHAIN_WIRING_v1_3_CANDIDATE.md §8]

ALONE
- What it is: ACCEPTED — Immediate application of the more restrictive current result across retrieval, formed output and future writes. [04/NH_B_INT_6_PRIVACY_FIRST_SACL_SECOND_OUTPUT_CHAIN_WIRING_v1_3_CANDIDATE.md §8]
- Takes in: ACCEPTED — Privacy restriction, SACL downgrade, PBR change, speaker change, addressed-stream change, Ness-presence loss, observability change, mode-generation change, close, suspension, step-up loss or restart. [04/NH_B_INT_6_PRIVACY_FIRST_SACL_SECOND_OUTPUT_CHAIN_WIRING_v1_3_CANDIDATE.md §8]
- Does: ACCEPTED — Applies the more restrictive result immediately and cancels stale retrieval and formed output. SACL compares the new level with each in-progress operation's material_sensitivity; if lower, flags immediate discard and sends the output-generation component the discard signal before any channel write. No partial output of that higher-sensitivity operation is delivered. Cancellation reaches exactly operations carrying mode_authority_dependency_ref on the affected session; separately authorized background work retains its own authority, while any later interactive output still needs current privacy, access and delivery checks. [04/NH_B_INT_6_PRIVACY_FIRST_SACL_SECOND_OUTPUT_CHAIN_WIRING_v1_3_CANDIDATE.md §8]
- Gives out: ACCEPTED — Immediate blocking/discard of affected work, followed by its record or carried-forward recording obligation. Existing proposed delivery_unknown remains unresolved; a later positive confirmation may still record historical delivery. [04/NH_B_INT_6_PRIVACY_FIRST_SACL_SECOND_OUTPUT_CHAIN_WIRING_v1_3_CANDIDATE.md §8] [04/NH_B_INT_6_PRIVACY_FIRST_SACL_SECOND_OUTPUT_CHAIN_WIRING_v1_3_CANDIDATE.md §6C]
- Must never: ACCEPTED — Wait for successful logging before restricting; replay a rejected/discarded draft; deliver under an old epoch or generation; sweep up independently authorized background work; reopen access because a restriction record is pending. [04/NH_B_INT_6_PRIVACY_FIRST_SACL_SECOND_OUTPUT_CHAIN_WIRING_v1_3_CANDIDATE.md §8]
- Fails closed by: ACCEPTED — Delivery stays blocked while the restriction record is written or carried forward; unknown earlier delivery cannot be relabeled failed, withheld or discarded. [04/NH_B_INT_6_PRIVACY_FIRST_SACL_SECOND_OUTPUT_CHAIN_WIRING_v1_3_CANDIDATE.md §8] [04/NH_B_INT_6_PRIVACY_FIRST_SACL_SECOND_OUTPUT_CHAIN_WIRING_v1_3_CANDIDATE.md §6C]

### C-SACL.31 — Delivery retries under current gates and B9 bounds
Stamp: ACCEPTED    Source: [04/NH_B_INT_6_PRIVACY_FIRST_SACL_SECOND_OUTPUT_CHAIN_WIRING_v1_3_CANDIDATE.md §9]

ALONE
- What it is: ACCEPTED — Output-attempt retry under stable identity, fresh authorization and accepted B9 retry policy. [04/NH_B_INT_6_PRIVACY_FIRST_SACL_SECOND_OUTPUT_CHAIN_WIRING_v1_3_CANDIDATE.md §9]
- Takes in: ACCEPTED — The original parent/key, exact immutable payload, current privacy/SACL decisions, current owner versions/fence and the actual retry class. [04/NH_B_INT_6_PRIVACY_FIRST_SACL_SECOND_OUTPUT_CHAIN_WIRING_v1_3_CANDIDATE.md §9]
- Does: ACCEPTED — Before any write, a technical retry keeps the same proposed output_operation_id and proposed delivery_idempotency_key while using a new proposed delivery_attempt_id and fresh proposed delivery_claim_id. Every attempt obtains current privacy, SACL, owner and fence checks against the exact payload again; changing facts belong to the attempt/claim, never the key. After an unknown result there is at most one safe automatic attempt, and only positive non-delivery proof or verified same-token channel idempotency can make it eligible. [04/NH_B_INT_6_PRIVACY_FIRST_SACL_SECOND_OUTPUT_CHAIN_WIRING_v1_3_CANDIDATE.md §9]
- Does: ACCEPTED — Consumes B9's two bounds, stopping at whichever is reached first: technical attempts at most 3 total, original plus 2 retries; minimum live-chat gaps 10 seconds then 30 seconds; minimum background/nightly gaps 1 minute then 3 minutes; elapsed maxima 7 minutes live and 15 minutes background/nightly, starting at the first failed attempt when the retry episode begins. Bad/unsafe/unsupported drafts are recorded rejected with their reason, then receive one careful immediate retry. Early stop is permitted if retry is clearly useless or unsafe. Beyond normal limits requires a real change, such as new memory, new Ness instruction, better context, repaired missing evidence, repaired tool/file/search problem or solved blocker; the examples are not exhaustive and repetition alone is not real change. [04/NH_B9_RETRY_VALUES_WIRING_INTO_B9_B10_BHOLD_B24_v1_4_CANDIDATE.md §3]
- Gives out: ACCEPTED — An eligible fresh child attempt or a stop with the reason, retained work record and unfinished state for later continuation only on real change. The output-specific unknown-result bound remains additionally restrictive. [04/NH_B9_RETRY_VALUES_WIRING_INTO_B9_B10_BHOLD_B24_v1_4_CANDIDATE.md §3] [04/NH_B_INT_6_PRIVACY_FIRST_SACL_SECOND_OUTPUT_CHAIN_WIRING_v1_3_CANDIDATE.md §9]
- Must never: ACCEPTED — Cache a gate pass across restriction, reuse stale/spent/invalidated claims, change duplicate scope after a fresh pass, retry confirmed delivery, blindly resend unknown delivery, report fake success, hide failure, retry endlessly or promote a rejected draft to final output. [04/NH_B_INT_6_PRIVACY_FIRST_SACL_SECOND_OUTPUT_CHAIN_WIRING_v1_3_CANDIDATE.md §9] [04/NH_B9_RETRY_VALUES_WIRING_INTO_B9_B10_BHOLD_B24_v1_4_CANDIDATE.md §3]
- Fails closed by: ACCEPTED — No retry after confirmed delivery. After uncertainty, no resend without the required channel fact, current gates and remaining bounds; exhaustion preserves unfinished state without unsafe completion. [04/NH_B_INT_6_PRIVACY_FIRST_SACL_SECOND_OUTPUT_CHAIN_WIRING_v1_3_CANDIDATE.md §9] [04/NH_B9_RETRY_VALUES_WIRING_INTO_B9_B10_BHOLD_B24_v1_4_CANDIDATE.md §3]

### C-SACL.34 — One output parent log with child history
Stamp: ACCEPTED    Source: [04/NH_B_INT_6_PRIVACY_FIRST_SACL_SECOND_OUTPUT_CHAIN_WIRING_v1_3_CANDIDATE.md §12]

ALONE
- What it is: ACCEPTED — §0B/B-INT-11 logging on every participating output side: one real operation, one parent log. [04/NH_B_INT_6_PRIVACY_FIRST_SACL_SECOND_OUTPUT_CHAIN_WIRING_v1_3_CANDIDATE.md §12]
- Takes in: ACCEPTED — The actual admission, owner decisions, retrieval, formation, transformation, dispatch, restriction, retry and recovery events. [04/NH_B_INT_6_PRIVACY_FIRST_SACL_SECOND_OUTPUT_CHAIN_WIRING_v1_3_CANDIDATE.md §12]
- Does: ACCEPTED — Admission creates proposed output_operation in proposed requested state. Privacy pre-eligibility and final privacy each retain §7Q/B7's own decision record plus proposed output_stage_event; SACL retrieval scope and final access each retain SACL's own record plus a proposed stage event. Retrieval retains LMAC's routing record in the shared operational log, with no LMAC store, plus proposed retrieval_intersection_record. Formation writes a proposed stage event and immutable proposed delivery_payload_ref; transformation writes a proposed stage event in proposed privacy_transform_required and a new proposed payload-reference version, then repeats final privacy before SACL. Fence revalidation writes a proposed stage event referencing the mode owner's fence. [04/NH_B_INT_6_PRIVACY_FIRST_SACL_SECOND_OUTPUT_CHAIN_WIRING_v1_3_CANDIDATE.md §12]
- Does: ACCEPTED — Reservation writes proposed delivery_claim_record with claim_status active for its intended attempt. Invalidation writes a separate proposed delivery_claim_state_event with invalidated, leaving the immutable claim untouched; a new attempt gets a new claim. Before contact, proposed delivery_dispatch_intent_event and a proposed claim-state event with spent are flushed. Accepted handoff writes proposed delivery_attempt_event with its intended attempt id, exact claim and intent references; channel acceptance is the owner's fact and the proposed coordinator records it without asserting visibility. [04/NH_B_INT_6_PRIVACY_FIRST_SACL_SECOND_OUTPUT_CHAIN_WIRING_v1_3_CANDIDATE.md §12]
- Does: ACCEPTED — Positive delivery writes proposed delivery_confirmation_receipt referencing attempt/claim and moves proposed output_operation to proposed delivered; positive non-delivery writes proposed delivery_non_delivery_receipt. Uncertainty writes proposed delivery_uncertainty_record and keeps the parent open in proposed delivery_unknown. Withholding records proposed withheld plus the refusing gate's reference; restriction records proposed discard_event and proposed discarded where the lifecycle permits it. Refused duplicate writes proposed duplicate_delivery_prevented with stable key, claim, attempt and any confirmation/idempotency result. Retry is an append-only child attempt under the same parent/key with fresh facts and B9 classification. Recovery writes proposed output_recovery_event. A fail-closed halt records proposed failed plus a proposed stage event, without overriding unknown-delivery exclusivity. [04/NH_B_INT_6_PRIVACY_FIRST_SACL_SECOND_OUTPUT_CHAIN_WIRING_v1_3_CANDIDATE.md §12] [04/NH_B_INT_6_PRIVACY_FIRST_SACL_SECOND_OUTPUT_CHAIN_WIRING_v1_3_CANDIDATE.md §6C]
- Gives out: ACCEPTED — References-only parent/child history; privacy and channel reality stay with their owners while the proposed coordinator owns its records. [04/NH_B_INT_6_PRIVACY_FIRST_SACL_SECOND_OUTPUT_CHAIN_WIRING_v1_3_CANDIDATE.md §12]
- Must never: ACCEPTED — Put private payload or withheld content in logs; give logs evidence weight or let a log be evidence for itself; create a new real operation to log that the log was logged; create second parents for stages, retries or recovery; restore a gate, fence or delivery right from history. [04/NH_B_INT_6_PRIVACY_FIRST_SACL_SECOND_OUTPUT_CHAIN_WIRING_v1_3_CANDIDATE.md §12]
- Fails closed by: ACCEPTED — Required recording failure never delays a restriction; delivery remains blocked while the record is written or carried forward. Stamp: ACCEPTED    Source: [04/NH_B_INT_6_PRIVACY_FIRST_SACL_SECOND_OUTPUT_CHAIN_WIRING_v1_3_CANDIDATE.md §13]

ALONE

- Does: ACCEPTED — The kernel resolves, carries, checks and records typed references; the owner decides, acts and commits. It checks presence, readability, type and the owner-prescribed order: privacy before relevance, and final privacy first then SACL/PBR. Per-use owner decisions are resolved at the owner's own seam immediately before the protected effect, neither demanded before the owner creates them nor weakened by coordination. Kernel duplicate prevention recognizes, skips and records duplicates structurally by identity; its keys do not contain mutable authorization facts. Its refusal of attempted duplicate visible delivery is additional to B-INT-6's independent fence. [04/NH_UNIFIED_DURABLE_OPERATION_KERNEL_MECHANICAL_DESIGN_v1_9_CANDIDATE.md §T] [04/NH_UNIFIED_DURABLE_OPERATION_KERNEL_MECHANICAL_DESIGN_v1_9_CANDIDATE.md §O]

B-INT-6 retains visible-output and duplicate identities, claims/attempts, immutable payload, privacy/SACL delivery decisions, proposed delivery_unknown and confirmed evidence. An unresolved owner result is represented only as missing durable required terminal evidence with the owner's own reference, never a kernel reclassification. [04/NH_UNIFIED_DURABLE_OPERATION_KERNEL_MECHANICAL_DESIGN_v1_9_CANDIDATE.md §C.1] [04/NH_UNIFIED_DURABLE_OPERATION_KERNEL_MECHANICAL_DESIGN_v1_9_CANDIDATE.md §U]

## Named review dispositions

The complete behavior was reviewed for misfiled restrictions, failure outcomes and gates, including every USED BY row. Each positive scan hit below is retained for its named reason.

| Card / line | Flag | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| C-SACL.2.1 — Access session identifier; line 308 | empty_together | session_id is a data slot in the containing session record. V10 declares no independent producer, gate or mutation for this field; its containing-record use is explicit. |
| C-SACL.2.2 — Last SIA event reference; line 331 | empty_together | last_sia_event_id is the session's stored reference. The source gives no separate field-level actor or authorization; the session record consumes it through its reciprocal row. |
| C-SACL.2.3 — Last SIA receipt time; line 354 | empty_together | last_sia_received_at is receipt-time data, not an independent process. No separate field-level relationship is decided; the containing session uses it explicitly. |
